reviews.review: It's a fun game and the co-op aspect of it is well done.  I do miss the old school AvP, back around 2000, being able to play as a Marine, alien, or Predator was cool, but this has a lot of that fun and the story is actually pretty interesting.

Three players, Three Marines, Three Colonial Marines, dropped into a meat grinder on an abandoned Space station, long believed lost. Sent to rescue a scientist, but not really given good intel on the mission. Discover, first hand, what it is like to be outnumbered, afraid, and reliant on your two fireteam buddies, as you delve deeper into the subterfuge of the Weyland-Yutani Corporation. Experience fear and horror, as your ammo count drops while your body count rises. Jump scares a-plenty as things move around you, rattle, bang, and clang, Xenomorphs of many shapes and sizes, and often in large numbers, swarm to your location, driven by bloodlust and thousands of years of instinct. To survive this horror, your bloodlust and survival instinct must be higher, your teamwork and cohesion must be stronger. Your will to live could be your only hope to survive this. Well, that, and your trusty M42A2 Armat Pulse Rifle and Kruger .50 calibre Pistol. Perhaps you want to be a Smart Gunner? A Medic? A Technician? If you have what it takes, the Colonial Marines need recruits. The UACM Needs YOU!

I'm just over 60 hours, and have never had so much fun being scared, running for my life, running out of ammo, standing shoulder to shoulder with my buddies, expecting to never see the light of day again! Replayability is high with this game too, as you level up your character, your role, your weapons, you will unlock more weapons, more paint schemes for those weapons, more decals to apply to those weapons, and more modules to apply to your perks kit. Emotes are unlockable, discoverable, and purchaseable, if you ever actually have the time to flex, dance, andgesture at each other. You really should concentrate on killing those things though, because you don't see them taunting each other! You can become the ultimate bad455 Marine in your Fireteam, or you could be torn to bloody shreds, or even the next host of a Xenomorph. The choice is ultimately yours. (Or possibly theirs...)

Oorah, Marines. State of the bad455 art!

Solid, has it's flaws and has potential. Thankfully also not a full priced game.  

Think Left 4 Dead but with Aliens and marines. Its cool to progress through the maps, shoot aliens, complete objectives and hold the line against an onslaught of enemies. The problem with this game is that there isn't an easy matchmaking, instead you have to pick the map and level you want to play and then you join a que for that specific map and level. Even if you beat the game, there is no quick play or just hoping into a group that needs another member. As the player count dies down, either your going to need to find groups offline or just play solo with bots and that is not fun. 

They have cool classes that each have a little spice to them. Classes are restricted based on abilities and certain types of gear. For example, your class might be limited to only using a handgun and a cqw weapon while another can use a rifle and a cqw. They balance this by having the classes have different and specific abilities. 

The potential lies in what they can do given an expansion/major update. Playing this game, you can see pretty easily how you might be able to play as a Predator. The demo class has an over the shoulder missile launcher that feels and looks like the predators shoulder mounted weapon. There is even a challenge card that gives you thermal vision (similar to predator vision) for a whole map.

I would love to see this turn into an Aliens vs Predator kind of game but honestly I'm not sure they are going that route. All in all though, it's solid but don't expect it to have a huge shelf life if it doesn't update it's matchmaking, add playable predator - alien gameplay and some sort of multiplayer like Left 4 Dead style vs mode.

down sides at the moment are that there are only 3 slots for a fireteam so your 4th friend misses out, also there is no in game chat support and this makes things hard for people joining fireteams with strangers, there are 4 chapters to the story with 3 missions in each, limits replayability, if you do not have a full fireteam you are given AI bots to "help" you, these bots are usually just as much of a hindrance as help, occasionally the Xenos animations stutter or lag, providing you with the task of shooting what could be alive or dead enemy and wasting highly needed ammo or allowing alive ones to get within attack range.

up sides. the game is visually amazing, having heard myself and friends say "wow" near the same time looking at some scenery. the classes to play are varied and have great diversity allowing for unique playstyles and different team composition, the missions feel different and challenging, there is even a escort mission that i didn't hate in this game.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite is an enjoyable experience at a 40 dollar price. Not too expensive for the amount of content you get. It's a simple Left 4 Dead style "Get from point A to point B without dyeing" game and has a few "Hold the position" style moments with massive hordes of enemies and multiple enemy types. They game can get a little repetitive but never really let you get "bored". But the games devs really payed attention to the lore of this game. A lot of Alien fans will see and discover some lore from both the movies and the books. Now, Squad up with 2 other friends, pick a class, and go shoot some Aliens.

Strong and simple horde shooter, feels refreshingly simple. A bit short maybe, but equally it's not bloated with unnecessary features many games come with. Doesn't matter to me that there are no cut-scenes or facial movements etc. To me, they focused on the right things and I'm happy with that. 

The solo experience would be hugely improved for me if the bots were made to stay behind you. Too often they bravely (stupidly) charge into the open, and my shotgun. They are bots, if I want glory hunters I'm sure they can be found in multiplayer. Please just keep them at the rear, out of the way and let them provide their supporting fire.

As with these sort of games, the replay value comes from levelling up, and challenging yourself to try harder difficulties and the challenge cards are a good addition also, if anything I'd like to have more cards from crates to use more. I prefer changes to enemies (e.g. runners are lesser prowlers over time restrictions). Might look silly, but being able to swap enemies would give replayability to me, some maintenance Joe synths crawling out of obvious alien holes or dropping from vents may look silly, but if anything that makes it more appealing!

It may be too early for me to take an informed judgement on difficulty scaling, as I've only tried Extreme a little. I would it if the enemies don't just get more health, as this feels the cheapest approach to increasing difficulty. I like that the weapons feel strong, which is lost if the basic fodder take too many shots. I would prefer significantly increased numbers than extra health. Like what WWZ are doing with the upcoming dlc, give me overwhelming hordes and more specials over more health, please! Again, too soon for me to tell, and that's just my preference. 

Each class feels strong and has a role to play, admittedly some are stronger than others (at least to me) but hopefully future updates will balance this. Nice variety of weapons which I think generally all feel good enough; at least on normal and perhaps up to intense. Look forward to additional content. 

Knows what it wants to be and doesn't try to be anything other than that, which I appreciate. Look forward to future additions and new, classes, maps and modes. A solid foundation from which to build upon as far as I'm concerned!

It is a game with a lot of potential. But in my opinion it still have quite a lot of areas of improvement.

Pros: 
- It is a very nice looking game. The models are accurate and look very good.
- The graphics are great.
- Difficulties are as expected and accurate. 
- Very competitive to get the best stats at the end.
- Fun to kill aliens!

Cons:
- The biggest con first, it is VERY repetitive. 
- Kind of leading on from the first one, every task is move, defend, move, defend, move, defend, escape.
- The UI and the perk menu is very confusing.
- Earn more decals than you do mods.
- Headshots do not do nearly enough damage.
- Some of the stronger enemies just feel like bullet sponges.

Overall, it is a good 3 player game but definitely needs more work put into it before it is work the price it currently is. 
Overall rating would be 4/10
